extension.description: Show DeepSeek API usage and balance in the VSCode status bar and dashboard.
command.setApiKey: DeepSeek Usage Monitor: Set API Key
config.sessionToken.description: Platform Session Token (Bearer ...). Required to query usage data. How to get it: sign in to platform.deepseek.com/usage → press F12 (or right-click → Inspect) → Network → reload the page → find the cost?start=xxx request → copy the value after Bearer in the Authorization request header.
config.cookie.description: Browser cookie string. Required for usage API authentication. Same steps as above; the Cookie request header usually sits right below Authorization.
config.proxy.description: HTTP proxy URL (optional). Set this when a proxy is required to reach the platform; leave it empty for a direct connection.
config.language.description: Language of the dashboard and extension messages (the text on the VSCode settings page follows VSCode's own display language).
config.statusBarItems.markdownDescriptio:
Which items the status bar shows (**array order = display order**); leave empty to show the icon only.

- `todayCost` — Today: xx.xx CNY
- `monthCost` — Month: xx.xx CNY
- `balance` — Balance: xx.xx CNY
- `todayTokens` — Today xxx tokens

Missing values are shown as `—` (today/month data needs Session Token & Cookie).
config.statusBarLabel.markdownDescriptio: Name shown in the status bar, `DeepSeek Usage` by default. It can be set to any text (VSCode icon syntax works, e.g. `$(rocket) DS usage`). **Leave it empty to show only the icon and the data.** Up to 64 characters.
config.statusBarCloseWhenActive.markdown:
Click the status bar item again to close the dashboard while it is in the foreground.

**When off (default)** clicking always opens the dashboard, or focuses it if it is already open.
config.refreshInterval.markdownDescripti: Auto-refresh interval (**in minutes**). Default `1`. Decimals are allowed (e.g. `0.5` = 30 seconds); set `0` to disable auto-refresh.
command.setDashboardBackground: DeepSeek Usage Monitor: Set Dashboard Background
command.clearDashboardBackground: DeepSeek Usage Monitor: Clear Dashboard Background
config.dashboardBackgroundColor.markdown: Custom dashboard background (only effective when no background image is set): a CSS color (`#0b1220`, `rgb(11,18,32)`) or a gradient (`linear-gradient(135deg,#0b1220,#1b2a4a)`); leave empty to follow the VSCode theme. To use an image, set it separately.
config.dashboardBackgroundDim.markdownDe: Dimming applied over the background image (`0`–`0.9`), which keeps the text readable. Affects the background image only.
config.dashboardCardOpacity.markdownDesc: Opacity of the card background when a custom background (image or color) is active (`0.3`–`1`). Lower values let the background show through, with less text contrast. No effect in high-contrast themes (cards stay opaque).
config.dashboardFontScale.markdownDescri: Dashboard font scale (`0.8`–`1.4`, default `1`). Affects the dashboard only; the status bar font is controlled by VSCode.
config.chartsItems.markdownDescription:
Which of the three bar charts the dashboard shows (**array order = dashboard order**); leave it empty to hide all charts.

- `cost` — Cost
- `requests` — API requests
- `tokens` — Tokens

Each chart’s colors are independent; all three use the official palette by default and can be customized separately.
config.timezone.markdownDescription:
Time zone used for requests and the dashboard. **Empty = follow the local machine's time zone.** It can also be set to any IANA zone name (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `America/New_York`) or a shorthand like `GMT+8` / `UTC-5`.

Takes effect immediately (data is refetched). Note: the official usage page is fixed to GMT+8, so with another zone the "today / this month" numbers may differ from the website.
config.chartColors.markdownDescription:
Colors of the three bar charts. Normally written by the “Colors” button on each chart, but it can also be edited directly. Shape: `{ "cost": { "mode": "official|model|mono", "modelColors": { "model": "#RRGGBB" }, "baseColor": "#RRGGBB" }, "requests": {...}, "tokens": {...} }`.

Because it is a setting, it migrates with VS Code Settings Sync and the “Export / Import Configuration” commands. Leave it empty to use each chart’s official palette.
